methodological_rigor.justification: Case-control serum biomarker study (71 EC, 62 controls) with RT-qPCR analysis of HOTAIR and miR-646. Appropriate RNA extraction and qPCR methodology with internal controls (GAPDH, U6). Statistical methods include Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman correlation with Bonferroni correction. However, no power calculation; no adjustment for multiple confounders (tumor grade, stage linkage weak); ROC analysis for optimal cut-offs but sensitivity/specificity modest (HOTAIR: 63.3%/61.2%; miR-646: 66.7%/72.7%). Small sample size limits precision.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 4 (observational case-control). Serum biomarker identified (HOTAIR elevated in EC; miR-646 reduced in advanced stages) but clinical utility not demonstrated. No survival correlation; no treatment response linkage. Authors acknowledge further validation in larger cohorts and exosomal expression needed. Proposed clinical application speculative.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE partially followed: objectives clear, patient selection criteria detailed, statistical methods stated with Bonferroni correction. However, power analysis absent; exclusion criteria listed but baseline matching details (age, BMI, smoking) sparse quantitatively. Primer sequences proprietary (not disclosed). No data availability statement; no raw data or supplementary tables deposition mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: HOTAIR and miR-646 in EC tissue studied previously (refs 21, 33). Present study measures serum levels—translating known tissue markers to body fluid. Modest novelty; confirmatory rather than discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear methods with detailed RNA extraction and qPCR protocols. Results organized with appropriate figures (ROC curves). Discussion contextualizes ncRNAs in cancer and acknowledges limitations. Some sections repetitive; generally readable but could be tightened.

key_strengths: First study measuring serum HOTAIR and miR-646 levels in endometrial cancer patients.
Appropriate RT-qPCR methodology with internal controls and Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.
ROC analysis identifying optimal cut-off values for classification.
Clear case-control design with demographic matching (age, BMI, smoking).
key_concerns: No power calculation; modest sample size (71 EC, 62 controls) limits precision.
No survival correlation; HOTAIR and miR-646 not linked to clinical outcomes (disease-free survival, overall survival not associated).
Spearman correlation between HOTAIR and miR-646 not significant; proposed regulatory interaction unconfirmed.
miR-646 reduction in advanced stages not strong (P=0.045) and lacks mechanistic explanation.
Authors explicitly state 'further validation in larger patient cohorts...necessary'; findings preliminary.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Small exploratory serum biomarker study identifying HOTAIR and miR-646 alterations in endometrial cancer but lacking clinical outcome validation and mechanistic insight. Modest diagnostic accuracy and exploratory design warrant major revisions: increase sample size, link to survival/treatment response, validate in independent cohort.
